title: Prayer and The Our Father Breakdown
summary: Prayer is the living relationship of the children of God with their Father, and the Our Father is the perfect prayer taught by Jesus, containing seven petitions that express all the desires and needs of the Christian life ordered to the glory of God and our salvation.

blocks.text: Introduction: The Nature of Prayer

Prayer is the raising of one's mind and heart to God or the requesting of good things from God. More deeply, it is the living relationship of the children of God with their Father who is good beyond measure, with his Son Jesus Christ, and with the Holy Spirit. Prayer is a covenant relationship between God and man in Christ. [CCC 2559, 2564]

Christian prayer is a personal relationship of the children of God with the Father, with his Son Jesus Christ, and with the Holy Spirit. The grace of the Kingdom is the union of the entire Holy Trinity with the whole human spirit. Prayer is the response of faith to the free promise of salvation and a response of love to the thirst of the only Son of God. [CCC 2565]
Pray without ceasing.

blocks.title: CCC 2559-2564: Living Relationship
blocks.text: Prayer is the living relationship of the children of God with their Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; it is a covenant relationship between God and man in Christ.
I. The Our Father: The Perfect Prayer

The Lord's Prayer, the Our Father, is the most perfect of prayers. In it, Jesus teaches us not only what to ask for but also the order in which to ask. It is the summary of the whole Gospel and is at the heart of the Scriptures. The Our Father is given to us in the context of the Sermon on the Mount. [CCC 2761-2762, 2765]

The Our Father has seven petitions: the first three concern the glory of the Father, and the last four present our needs to him. The first three petitions draw us toward God's glory, while the last four express our human needs and desires. This order teaches us to seek first the Kingdom of God and his righteousness. [CCC 2765, 2803]

Pray then like this: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, On earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our debts, As we also have forgiven our debtors; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil.

blocks.title: CCC 2761-2762: Most Perfect Prayer
blocks.text: The Our Father is the most perfect prayer, teaching us not only what to ask but the order; it is the summary of the whole Gospel with seven petitions.
II. Our Father Who Art in Heaven

We begin by invoking God as Our Father, which expresses our new relationship with God through Baptism. We dare to call God Father because Jesus has revealed him to us and made us his adopted children. The word Our expresses our communion with all the baptized and our common hope. [CCC 2777, 2789-2790]

Who art in heaven does not refer to a place but to God's majesty and his presence in the hearts of the just. Heaven is the Father's house, our true homeland toward which we are journeying. To be in heaven is to be with Christ, where our life is hidden with God in Christ. [CCC 2794-2796]
For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the spirit of sonship. When we cry, Abba! Father!

blocks.title: CCC 2777: Adopted Sons
blocks.text: We call God Our Father because Jesus revealed him and made us adopted children; Our expresses communion with all the baptized and our common hope.
III. Hallowed Be Thy Name

The first petition is that God's name be hallowed, that is, recognized as holy and treated with reverence. God's name is holy because God himself is holy. We ask that his name be sanctified in us and in all people, that all may know, bless, and glorify him. [CCC 2807, 2809]

This petition is fulfilled when we live holy lives that bear witness to God's holiness. It is also eschatological, looking forward to the day when every knee shall bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. We ask that God's name be glorified in the Church and in the world. [CCC 2810, 2819]
You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be hallowed among the people of Israel. I am the LORD who hallow you.

blocks.title: CCC 2807: God's Name Holy
blocks.text: We ask that God's name be recognized as holy and treated with reverence, sanctified in us and all people, that all may know, bless, and glorify him.
IV. Thy Kingdom Come

The second petition looks to the coming of God's Kingdom, which was inaugurated by Christ and will be fulfilled at his return in glory. We pray for the growth of the Church and the spread of the Gospel. We also pray for the final coming of the Kingdom when God will be all in all. [CCC 2816, 2818, 2820]

This petition awakens in us the desire for the Kingdom and the hope of Christ's return. It calls us to work for justice, peace, and holiness in the world. The Kingdom of God is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. [CCC 2817, 2820]
He who testifies to these things says, Surely I am coming soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!

blocks.title: CCC 2816: Kingdom of God
blocks.text: We pray for the coming of God's Kingdom, inaugurated by Christ and to be fulfilled at his return; we desire the Kingdom and work for justice, peace, and holiness.
V. Thy Will Be Done on Earth as in Heaven

The third petition asks that God's will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In heaven, the angels and saints do God's will perfectly and joyfully. We ask for the grace to discern and do God's will on earth with the same love and obedience. [CCC 2822, 2824]

This petition requires humility, trust, and surrender to God's providence. It unites us to Christ, who said not my will, but yours be done. Doing God's will is the path to true freedom and happiness. [CCC 2825-2826]
And going a little farther he fell on his face and prayed, saying, My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt.

blocks.title: CCC 2822: God's Will
blocks.text: We ask that God's will be done on earth as in heaven, with humility and surrender, united to Christ who perfectly did the Father's will.
VI. Give Us This Day Our Daily Bread

The fourth petition expresses our trust in God's providence for our material and spiritual needs. Daily bread refers not only to food but to all that is necessary for life, including the Eucharist, the Bread of Life. We ask for what is necessary, not for excess or luxury. [CCC 2828, 2830, 2837]

This petition teaches us detachment from worldly goods and solidarity with the poor. It calls us to work honestly and to share with those in need. We pray for the bread of this day, trusting that God will provide for tomorrow as well. [CCC 2831, 2839]
Jesus said to them, I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst.

blocks.title: CCC 2828: Daily Bread
blocks.text: We ask for our daily bread, trusting in God's providence for material and spiritual needs, including the Eucharist; this teaches detachment and solidarity with the poor.
VII. Forgive Us Our Trespasses

The fifth petition acknowledges our sinfulness and our need for God's mercy. We ask forgiveness for our sins, which offend God and wound our communion with him and the Church. This petition is linked to the next clause, as we forgive those who trespass against us. [CCC 2838-2839, 2843]

God's mercy cannot penetrate our hearts unless we have forgiven those who have offended us. This petition challenges us to examine our hearts for bitterness or resentment. Forgiveness is the condition for receiving God's forgiveness and for our prayers to be heard. [CCC 2840, 2842]
For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father also will forgive you; but if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

blocks.title: CCC 2838-2839: Forgiveness
blocks.text: We ask forgiveness for our sins, acknowledging our need for mercy; God's mercy cannot penetrate our hearts unless we have forgiven those who offended us.
VIII. Lead Us Not Into Temptation

The sixth petition asks God not to allow us to be led into temptation. God does not tempt anyone to sin, but he permits trials that test and strengthen our faith. We ask for the grace to recognize temptation and the strength to resist it through prayer and vigilance. [CCC 2846-2847, 2849]

This petition awakens us to spiritual combat and the need for watchfulness. It calls us to pray for the discernment of spirits and for the strength to choose the good. We ask for the Holy Spirit's guidance to avoid occasions of sin and to persevere in grace. [CCC 2848, 2850]

No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your strength, but with the temptation will also provide the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

blocks.title: CCC 2846-2847: Spiritual Combat
blocks.text: We ask not to be led into temptation; God permits trials that test faith, and we ask for grace to recognize and resist temptation through prayer and vigilance.
IX. Deliver Us From Evil

The seventh petition asks deliverance from evil, which includes sin, Satan, and all the consequences of evil in the world. We pray for liberation from the power of the evil one and for protection against his attacks. This petition expresses our hope in Christ's victory over sin and death. [CCC 2850-2851, 2853]

We ask for the peace of Christ and the grace to persevere in hope until his return. This petition looks forward to the final victory when God will wipe away every tear and there will be no more death or mourning. We pray for the salvation of all and the triumph of God's Kingdom. [CCC 2852-2853]
But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from evil.

blocks.title: CCC 2850-2851: Deliverance
blocks.text: We ask deliverance from evil, sin, and Satan; we pray for liberation from the evil one and protection against his attacks, hoping in Christ's victory.
X. The Doxology: For Thine Is the Kingdom

The final doxology, For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever, is not in the earliest manuscripts of Matthew but is found in the ancient liturgical tradition of the Church. It is a fitting conclusion that returns all glory to God. The doxology expresses our confidence that God hears our prayers. [CCC 2760, 2855]

This doxology acknowledges that all power and glory belong to God alone. It is an act of adoration and praise, recognizing God's sovereignty over all creation. The liturgy concludes the Our Father with this doxology, and the people respond Amen, meaning so be it. [CCC 2855-2856]
Yours, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty; for all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours.

blocks.title: CCC 2855: Doxology
blocks.text: The doxology returns all glory to God, acknowledging his sovereignty; it is an act of adoration and praise, concluding with Amen, meaning so be it.
XI. Praying the Our Father Daily

The Our Father is the prayer of the Church par excellence, prayed in the Liturgy of the Hours and at every Mass. The faithful are encouraged to pray it frequently throughout the day, especially in the morning and evening. It is a perfect prayer for personal devotion and family prayer. [CCC 2768, 2774]

Praying the Our Father slowly and meditatively allows each petition to sink deep into our hearts. We can pause after each phrase to reflect on its meaning and apply it to our lives. The saints prayed the Our Father many times daily, finding in it inexhaustible riches. [CCC 2768, 2774]
Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving.

blocks.title: CCC 2768: Prayer of the Church
blocks.text: The Our Father is the prayer of the Church, prayed in the Liturgy and at Mass; the faithful are encouraged to pray it frequently, slowly and meditatively.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer: The Our Father
blocks.text: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, On earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our trespasses, As we forgive those who trespass against us; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil. Amen.
